question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class agent-scoped web/tool credential contract, and should it live under `agents.list[].tools.web`, a generic per-agent plugin/tool config surface, or remain global/plugin-scoped?
rationale: The chosen config location and precedence define a credential isolation boundary across web-search providers, SecretRefs, plugin-owned `webSearch`, provider auto-detection, config.apply, docs, and upgrade behavior, so automation cannot safely choose it.

options.title: Design generic agent-scoped credential/config contract
options.body: Add a shared contract for agent-scoped tool/provider/plugin settings with explicit precedence, SecretRef handling, validation, reload, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Add only `agents.list[].tools.web`
options.body: Solve the immediate web-search credential use case faster, but accept a narrower surface that may later conflict with plugin-owned web provider configuration.

options.title: Keep web credentials global
options.body: Leave web-search credentials as gateway-wide/plugin-scoped settings and document separate gateways or provider-specific workarounds for billing isolation.

recommendation.title: Design generic agent-scoped credential/config contract
recommendation.body: Add a shared contract for agent-scoped tool/provider/plugin settings with explicit precedence, SecretRef handling, validation, reload, docs, and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans strict config schema policy, SecretRef credential handling, and provider/plugin config boundaries where recent history points most strongly to steipete.
